title: Security by construction claims and their evidence
status_rationale: Echelon has no production deployment; the relevant rules exist only in the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1 or Unbound requirements, so this is a target state.
target_answer: Echelon publishes, per release, an architectural assurance matrix that classifies each property as proven, structurally enforced, empirically tested or unverified, with scope, exclusions (trusted infrastructure, stored procedures, interop, generated bundles, third-party scripts), the enforcing mechanism and the bypass tests. No elimination claim is made without scoped, reproducible evidence, and structural claims are independently tested for bypass before they are used to reduce any other testing.
current_practice: The Secure Construction Standard v0.1 (proposed) states the structural rules and the matrix as a deliverable. No matrix, bypass test or enforcing analyzer exists. Several components the Standard assigns (Aegis as rule registry, Vigila as runtime monitoring) have different verified purposes.

challenge.customer_intent: Have confidence that whole classes of vulnerability cannot occur, not just that none were found.
challenge.adverse_outcome: An overstated elimination claim leads customers and testers to skip testing a class that is in fact present.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Conventional programs detect instances after construction; they rarely claim class elimination.
challenge.contractually_required: No; customers ask for test results, not construction claims.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Achievable within a precisely defined scope when the unsafe operation is unavailable and every bypass path is enumerated and tested.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Restricted interfaces, compiler settings, analyzers and release gates.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Per-release matrix with bypass test results.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Construction plus scoped claims plus independent bypass testing.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, if fixtures and analyzers are published and reproducible, and an independent party attempts bypass.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Any unscanned path: trusted infrastructure code, stored procedures, interop, generated bundles, third-party scripts, administrative tools.
challenge.alternative_cost: Upfront interface and analyzer engineering, plus independent verification.
challenge.alternative_risks: Institutional overconfidence; enforcing components owned by Echelon itself are a single point of failure.
supporting_arguments: Prevention is cheaper than repeated detection.
Scoped claims are falsifiable and therefore testable.

agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Technical reviewers may value it; risk and procurement functions will treat it as first-party until independently verified.'; institutional acceptance rating 'uncertain' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Several enforcing components do not exist or have different verified purposes.
First-party claims about first-party tools lack independence.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Explicit domain states and validated domain types
status_rationale: Echelon has no production deployment; the relevant rules exist only in the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1 or Unbound requirements, so this is a target state.
target_answer: Security-relevant values (amounts, EINs, routing numbers, tenant identifiers, authority grants) are types whose constructors validate and are private; workflow states are explicit discriminated unions with only legal transitions representable; exhaustive matching is compiler-enforced with warnings as errors; state machines and invariants are property-tested. Echelon is explicit that types prove representability, not that the encoded policy is the right one.

title: Database access architecture and dynamic SQL elimination
status_rationale: Echelon has no production deployment; the relevant rules exist only in the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1 or Unbound requirements, so this is a target state.
target_answer: Only the application's restricted typed interface and Strata-governed schema deployments touch authoritative databases. Each sponsor tenant has its own schema and role with row-level security; authoritative tables are insert-only for the application role; database functions contain no dynamic SQL; administrative roles are break-glass only with two-person activation; Strata drift checks cover grants, triggers and policies and block release on 'not-compared' or 'unverifiable' states. The scope of the no-dynamic-SQL claim, including stored procedures, migrations, reporting and trusted infrastructure, is stated with evidence.
current_practice: Strata exists as a pilot declarative schema tool for PostgreSQL 16 with explicit not-compared and unverifiable states (strata@c6a384ec). It does not provide a runtime query interface. No Unbound database exists.
intended_practice: Only the application's restricted typed interface and Strata-governed schema deployments touch authoritative databases. Each sponsor tenant has its own schema and role with row-level security; authoritative tables are insert-only for the application role; database functions contain no dynamic SQL; administrative roles are break-glass only with two-person activation; Strata drift checks cover grants, triggers and policies and block release on 'not-compared' or 'unverifiable' states. The scope of the no-dynamic-SQL claim, including stored procedures, migrations, reporting and trusted infrastructure, is stated with evidence.

challenge.customer_intent: Ensure nobody, including Echelon engineers and tools, can alter financial records outside governed paths.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Injection or direct tampering with ledger data.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Parameterized queries plus DBA access controls are effective but rarely cover database-side dynamic SQL and administrative tooling comprehensively.
challenge.legally_required: No specific technique; safeguards rules require reasonable access control.
challenge.historical_convention: ORM, DBA roles, periodic access review.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Within scope if all connection paths are enumerated and database functions are inspected; trusted infrastructure and stored procedures are the usual gaps.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Role grants declared in Strata, drift detection, analyzer over SQL source.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Strata drift status per release and grant export.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Declared grants plus insert-only roles plus drift gating.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes from catalog exports and Strata output.

challenge.invalidating_conditions: A reporting or support tool with direct database credentials; a function using EXECUTE with concatenated input; a PostgreSQL major version Strata does not support.
challenge.alternative_cost: Strata maturation from pilot; Unbound ledger component.
challenge.alternative_risks: Pilot-status tool on the critical path.
supporting_arguments: Strata's explicit unknown states avoid false clean diffs.

title: Browser architecture: no user HTML and no application script outside Limen
status_rationale: Echelon has no production deployment; the relevant rules exist only in the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1 or Unbound requirements, so this is a target state.
target_answer: The browser runs only Limen's kernel and application logic compiled to WebAssembly, which has no DOM access; the kernel binds data through a small set of declared attributes; no user HTML is accepted; no third-party script is loaded unless inventoried, approved and pinned by digest; every release inventories scripts, WebAssembly modules and interop exports and checks generated bundles for unsafe sinks. Limen itself is reviewed and tested as security-critical code.
current_practice: Limen exists (limen@743cdb9b): a dependency-free TypeScript browser kernel and protocol with F# WebAssembly consumers including a product site; it has an architecture check script and CODEOWNERS guardrails. No Unbound UI exists and Limen has had no independent security review.
intended_practice: The browser runs only Limen's kernel and application logic compiled to WebAssembly, which has no DOM access; the kernel binds data through a small set of declared attributes; no user HTML is accepted; no third-party script is loaded unless inventoried, approved and pinned by digest; every release inventories scripts, WebAssembly modules and interop exports and checks generated bundles for unsafe sinks. Limen itself is reviewed and tested as security-critical code.

challenge.customer_intent: Prevent script injection and malicious third-party code in the browser.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Session hijacking, credential theft or display manipulation through injected or supply-chain script.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Framework encoding, CSP and script inventories are effective when maintained; third-party scripts are a common failure.
challenge.legally_required: No; PCI DSS 6.4.3 requires script inventory and authorization on payment pages only.
challenge.historical_convention: SPA framework with many npm dependencies, CSP optional.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Reduces application script to one small kernel; does not eliminate script, and the WebAssembly runtime loader and interop glue are generated JavaScript.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Kernel confinement plus inventory plus CSP.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes for inventory; kernel correctness needs independent review.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Adding analytics, chat or payment widgets; partner embedding requiring host-page script.
challenge.alternative_cost: Limen maintenance as a single critical component.
challenge.alternative_risks: Concentration risk in Limen; WebAssembly debugging tools are less mature for security testers.
supporting_arguments: Dramatically smaller script surface than typical SPAs.
agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely as design; testers will still test.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Script still exists in the kernel; the claim moves rather than removes the surface.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.
